newsitem.title: USA: Abducted Michigan schoolgirls found in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Abducted Michigan schoolgirls found in Florida.

text.p: Two young sisters missing since they stepped off a school bus last Friday were found unhurt on Tuesday morning in Daytona Beach, Florida, as their three abductors were arrested.
Teresa Hainer, 9, and Jessica Hainer, 6, of Galesburg, Michigan, were the subject of a four-day nationwide search that involved thousands of law enforcement officials.

"The girls are safe," FBI Special Agent Joseph Martinolich told a news conference in Kalamazoo. "We were told by the agents at the scene that they're none the worse for the wear. Maybe a little tired, a little bedraggled, maybe dishevelled, but they're in good shape."
The girls were bathed, given medical examinations and were brought to state child counsellors Tuesday as arrangements were made to fly them back as early as Tuesday night, officials said.
Television footage showed them cradling large teddy bears as they got into a van late Tuesday afternoon.

Police in Daytona Beach arrested the three suspects -- acquaintances of the girls' father -- without incident about 9:30 a.m. (1430 GMT) as they and the girls entered a gift shop on the Daytona beachfront strip.

A college missionary from Cambridge, Massachusetts, spoke to the suspects and the girls at length Monday and later that night called police after she recognised their pictures on television newscasts.
"I met them out on the beach. They looked kind of scruffy," said Loh-Sze Leung, 20, a Harvard University student who was in Daytona with an evangelical group that talks to students about God.
"The girls seemed kind of unhappy or shy. But nothing seemed wrong. They didn't look like they were on the run or anything," she said.

Ronald Stafford, 21, his brother Lee Stafford, 17, and Ricky Geer, 19, were arrested on federal kidnapping charges. They also will be charged with kidnapping under Michigan state law, which will allow Lee Stafford to be tried as an adult.
Court records showed that Ronald Stafford spent three years in an adolescent sex-offender programme.
Martinolich said the men made no demand for money and their motive for abducting the girls is still "in the realm of speculation."
Geer told reporters as he was being led to a police van for transport to a federal detention centre that he did not know the girls had been kidnapped.
Asked why the men had the girls, Geer said, "I don't know. I was picked up downtown (in Kalamazoo) and I was asked if I wanted to go to Florida. As far as I know, it was Ron's daughters."
The girls' father, 33-year-old Jesse Hainer, did not speak to reporters at the news conference. He is divorced from the girls' mother but has full custody.
Olivia Hainer, the girls' grandmother, thanked the "G-men" who located Teresa and Jessica and said she planned a big welcome home celebration for them.
"My girls like lots of sweets, so I'll probably go home and bake lots of pies and cupcakes and everything else for them so they know grandma's still around and still loves them," Hainer said.

The two schoolgirls were supposed to go to a babysitter's home when they were dropped off at a Galesburg trailer park on Friday afternoon, but a man waiting for the bus told them to get into a 1988 Pontiac 6000 station wagon instead.
Police and witnesses said the girls at first did not want to go, but eventually got into the car anyway.

Galesburg-Augusta School District Superintendent Ronald Mrozinski defended the bus driver's actions in letting the girls off the bus, saying that she acted in a "professional, planned manner in accordance with all of our specifications."
